toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Verbrand' is the usual transitive verb for using up fuel and matches 'aanhou verbrand' and 'wat ons verbrand' later in the lesson.
toegepas.fout: 'brand ... steenkool' is a loose transitive use where Afrikaans uses 'verbrand' for consuming fuel, and the lesson itself says 'verbrand' twice later.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The more exact verb, consistent with the rest of the lesson, with no change in meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: The lesson and the hidro-elektries definition say 'stromende water' and 'water wat stroom', so one word for the same thing is clearer for the learner.
toegepas.fout: The lesson calls the same thing 'stromende water' and 'water wat stroom' everywhere else, including the shared definition, so 'vloeiende' is the only different word for it.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Using one word for one thing helps a Grade 6 reader, and the meaning stays the same.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS writes compounds as one word; this compound is not long or unclear enough to need a hyphen.
toegepas.fout: The hyphen is not needed; AWS writes this compound as one word.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A spelling fix that leaves the protected name 'kragstasie' whole.

toegepas.voor: Die sonpaneel is die een wat heeltemal anders werk.
toegepas.na: Die sonpaneel werk heeltemal anders as die ander twee.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'is die een wat' copies English 'is the one that'; the direct verb with 'as die ander twee' keeps the contrast with wind and water more naturally.
toegepas.fout: 'is die een wat heeltemal anders werk' copies English 'is the one that' and reads stiffly.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The direct verb with 'as die ander twee' is natural, and it only spells out the contrast with wind and water that the context already sets up.

toegepas.voor: Niks draai en niks brand nie.
toegepas.na: Niks draai nie, en niks brand nie.
toegepas.rede_vinder: Two clauses with their own subject and verb each need their own closing 'nie', and AWS puts a comma before 'en' between them.
toegepas.fout: Two clauses, each with its own subject and verb, share one closing 'nie', and there is no AWS comma before 'en'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Each clause gets its own negation and the AWS comma goes in, with the meaning unchanged.

toegepas.voor: Dit maak net elektrisiteit solank die lig daarop val.
toegepas.na: Dit maak elektrisiteit net solank die lig daarop val.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'net elektrisiteit' can read as 'only electricity'; placing 'net' before 'solank' makes it limit the time, which is the intended meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'maak net elektrisiteit' can read as 'makes only electricity' rather than 'only while the light falls on it'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Moving 'net' in front of 'solank' fixes the ambiguity in favour of the meaning intended, which matches the sonpaneel definition.

laat_vaar.voor: Die wind hou op en begin later weer waai.
laat_vaar.na: Die wind gaan lê en begin later weer waai.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Die wind gaan lê' is the natural Afrikaans idiom for wind dying down; the meaning is unchanged.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Hou op en begin later weer waai' is a clean pair and already reads well; 'gaan lê' means dying down rather than stopping, so it is a sideways move that also shifts the meaning slightly.

laat_vaar.blok: Water wat van hoog af stroom
laat_vaar.voor: deur groot pype af na turbines
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'af ... laer af' repeats the particle in one short sentence; 'stroom ... na turbines wat laer af staan' already says the water goes down.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'deur groot pype af' is natural Afrikaans and carries the downward movement of the water; dropping 'af' loses that for a small gain in style.

na_skrywer.voor: 'n Sonpaneel maak snags niks en minder wanneer dit bewolk is.
na_skrywer.na: 'n Sonpaneel maak snags geen elektrisiteit nie, en minder wanneer dit bewolk is.
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'maak snags niks en minder' is a compressed, ambiguous construction without the negative 'nie'; naming what it makes and closing the negation reads clearly.
na_skrywer.fout: 'maak snags niks en minder wanneer dit bewolk is' is missing its closing 'nie' and squeezes two ideas into one sentence, so it makes a reader stumble.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but the proposal puts a comma before 'en' in front of a fragment with no subject or verb of its own, which breaks the AWS rule, so the writer should repair the sentence another way.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: solank ons dit nie vinniger gebruik as wat die natuur dit aanvul nie
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: In the block 'Wat die natuur weer aanvul' this protected clause follows 'Hulle raak nie op nie', so the singular 'dit' twice refers back to the plural 'hulle' (son, wind, water); a person may want 'hulle' in this lesson's study text, though the wording is fine inside the glossary definition where the subject is singular.
